chunks: And by his chain, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to Musa: 'Make your tongue behind your heart, you will be safe, and frequent My remembrance by night and day, and do not follow the sin in its quarry for you will regret, for the sin is a provision for the people of the Fire.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of keeping the tongue behind the heart in Shia teachings?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this Hadith Qudsi emphasizes the spiritual discipline of aligning speech with inner consciousness ('tongue behind the heart') to preserve divine safety. It links consistent dhikr with proactive sin avoidance, illustrating the Shia concept that minor transgressions, if unchecked, become the 'mine' or source of eternal punishment.

en.hubeali: And by his chain, from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said to Musa<sup>as</sup>: “Make your<sup>as</sup> tongue to be behind your heart, you<sup>as</sup> will be safe, and frequent My<sup>azwj</sup> Mention by the night and the day, and do not follow the sin in its quarry for you<sup>as</sup> will regret, for the sin is a provision for the people of the Fire’.
en.sarwar: 10. Through the same chain of narrators it is narrated from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said to Moses, ‘Keep your tongue behind your heart and you will remain safe. Speak of Me very often during the day and night. Do not follow a sin in its pit (sinful people) or you will regret. Sin is the promised place of the people of fire.’”
